scenes.prompt: Commissioned editorial photography for Dwell magazine, modern-architecture spread; NOT a product render, NOT advertising, NOT stock. Hasselblad X2D 100C, 45mm f/2.8, aperture priority. A poured-concrete residential staircase, mid-century California home, late afternoon. The 86mm recessed LED step light sits flush in the baseboard wall at ankle height on the third riser — a small white-framed square barely distinguishable from the wall plane, emitting a narrow 30-degree warm wash across the concrete tread. Concrete shows hairline shrinkage cracks and a faint dust film along the riser edge. Paint on the adjacent baseboard is chipped at one corner. Exposure is committed: the staircase upper landing clips to near-white in the window light; the lower treads stay genuinely dark. Zero color cast — the warm LED glow stays strictly local to the tread surface, concrete reads true cool grey elsewhere. Kodak Portra 400 grain throughout, 2% corner vignette, 1px chromatic aberration at the blown window edge. Palette: raw concrete grey, off-white, warm amber (local only), matte black handrail, dusty sage wall. No people, no alcohol. The fixture matches the variant reference image exactly — finish and form as shown.
scenes.cameraAngle: low angle, eye-level with ankle height

Commissioned editorial photography for World of Interiors magazine, eclectic-townhouse spread; NOT a product render, NOT advertising, NOT stock. Hasselblad 907X 50C, 65mm f/3.2, aperture priority. A Victorian London townhouse staircase, late evening. Painted timber stair risers in faded Farrow & Ball off-white; the 86mm recessed LED step light is set flush in the plaster wall at ankle height beside the fourth riser, its white-finish frame nearly flush with the slightly uneven plaster surface. It casts a warm-white glow across the worn stair carpet runner. The runner shows a frayed edge at one tread; the plaster beside the fixture has a hairline crack and a faint scuff from a moved piece of furniture. Paint on the adjacent skirting board is yellowed and chipped near the newel post. Exposure is committed: the upper landing window light clips to pure white; the under-stair alcove stays black. Zero color cast — warm LED glow is strictly local to the runner surface, off-white plaster reads true in ambient incandescent. Kodak Portra 400 grain, 2% corner vignette, 1px chromatic aberration at the blown landing window. Palette: faded off-white, worn burgundy runner, warm amber (local only), aged oak newel, shadow black. No people, no alcohol.
